shared_elements: fanged/toothed predator or beast head shown frontally at the top
anthropomorphic figure with head and schematic arms placed below the beast head
figures stacked vertically one above another in registers
row of repeated animal heads / repeated motifs
schematic hands or limbs bent inward toward the body
large staring eyes rendered as ovals
justification: Both surfaces present a vertically stacked hierarchy in which a toothed, wide-mouthed predatory head occupies the top and an anthropomorphic figure with schematic inward-bent arms and large oval eyes sits directly beneath it, a fairly specific and arbitrary combination rather than a generic animal-plus-human pairing. The main difference is that B additionally carries a whole population of secondary creatures (birds, snake-like and long-necked animals, a squatting figure) spread over a flat surface in bands, while A is reduced to just two or three superimposed heads/bodies with no accompanying fauna.
